observed_original_abi.calling_convention_observation: 0x00b8d970 is 8b 41 2c, MOV EAX,[ECX + 0x2c]: the ModRM byte 41 is mod=01 disp8 reg=000, so the receiver is ECX with an 8-bit displacement. EDX is used as scratch by the SHR. There is no stack argument, no frame and the epilogue is a bare RET, so the caller owns all stack cleanup.
observed_original_abi.return_semantics: Bit 8 of the flag word at receiver+0x2c, materialised as a full dword that is exactly 0 or exactly 1. SHR EAX,8 first clears bits 0..7 and bit 31, then AND AL,1 clears bits 8..31, so the whole register ends up 0 or 1 and the upper three bytes are provably zero.
observed_original_abi.return_observation: 0x00b8d973 SHR EAX,0x8 followed by 0x00b8d976 AND AL,0x1 leaves the full dword as 0 or 1. Consumers agree: 0x00c8b878 and 0x00c48534 and 0x00c44d0c all use TEST AL,AL, which is compatible with either width, but the reconstruction was written to the dword contract rather than the byte one and the model test pins it.
observed_original_abi.hidden_this_register: ECX, read once and never modified

layout.padding_after: 0x00b8d979 through 0x00b8d97f are seven cc bytes (INT3 inter-function pad), confirmed by the 16-byte live read
layout.frame_shape: none: no PUSH, no SUB ESP, no MOV EBP,ESP, no register save or restore
layout.writes: nothing: EAX only, no memory write anywhere in the program address space

observed_mechanics: 0x00b8d970: 8b 41 2c - MOV EAX,[ECX + 0x2c] loads the whole 32-bit flag word; the ModRM disp8 0x2c is the field offset.
0x00b8d973: c1 e8 08 - SHR EAX,0x8 is a logical right shift by 8, so bit 8 of the original word becomes bit 0 of EAX and bits 0..7 plus bit 31 are discarded.

0x00b8d976: 24 01 - AND AL,0x1 masks only the low byte, and because the SHR already zeroed bits 8..31 the whole register is reduced to 0 or 1. AND AL,1 rather than AND EAX,1 is what makes the upper three bytes provably zero.
0x00b8d978: c3 - RET with no immediate, so the callee pops zero stack words.
Live memory read at 0x00b8d970 returns 8b412cc1e8082401c3cccccccccccccccccc, confirming all four instructions and the pad.

The inlined duplicate at 0x00b8d9ff..0x00b8da12 is the decisive corroboration: on the SAME field +0x2c it performs EAX = [ESI + 0x2c] ; SHR EAX,8 ; TEST AL,1 ; JNZ, an exact inlining of this function, and then at 0x00b8da12 separately tests bit 0x800 of the same word with TEST dword ptr [ESI + 0x2c],0x800. Two independent bit positions in one 32-bit word is what proves +0x2c is a packed flag word and that bit 8 is a flag rather than data.
0x00c8b873: CALL 0x00b8d970 ; 0x00c8b878 TEST AL,AL ; 0x00c8b87a JNZ 0x00c8b905, so the answer is a gate that skips the rest of the loop body.
0x00c44d07: CALL 0x00b8d970 ; 0x00c44d0c TEST AL,AL ; 0x00c44d0e JNZ 0x00c44ec3, an early return from the caller.

0x00c4852f and 0x00c48548 in caller 0x00c484e0 both dispatch this function on ECX = [ESI + 0x9c] + 0x13c and [ESI + 0x1e8] + 0x13c respectively, and each is followed by TEST AL,AL ; JNZ 0x00c48591, so the same flag is consulted on two different sub-objects before the caller commits to state 1.

clang++ -m32 -O2 with __attribute__((thiscall)) emits 8b 41 2c c1 e8 08 83 e0 01 c3 for the reconstruction: the same 9 bytes, the same offsets, the same instruction sequence; the only difference is that clang prefers AND EAX,1 over AND AL,1, which for a full-dword result is semantically identical.

Its body chains 0x00b3d2a0, 0x00bb99e0, 0x00feb9f0, 0x00fee220 and 0x00c4b220 and was not fully resolved in this batch.

semantic_contract: Return bit 8 of the 32-bit flag word at receiver+0x2c, as a full dword that is exactly 0 or exactly 1. The extraction is a logical right shift by 8 followed by a mask of 1, so the function is a pure bit test: no guard, no clamp, no callee, no global read, no side effect and no branch. The receiver is not null-checked. The neighbouring state field at receiver+0x2c's offset minus 4, i.e. +0x28, is not consulted here; callers check it themselves and skip this function entirely for state values 0 and 1.
classification_rationale: Not STRONG_SEMANTIC: the body is complete and the ABI, the offset, the shift amount, the mask, the return width and the bit index are all OBSERVED, and the bitfield nature of the field is corroborated by an inlined duplicate rather than assumed; but the owning class and the game meaning of flag bit 8 are not established, and that is a material element. Not STRUCTURAL_ONLY: the behavioural contract is a specific bit extraction with a specific index, fully determined and reconstructed. The bound is named: owning type and the meaning of bit 8.
semantic_findings: This is a named-bit accessor, not a data accessor: the SHR-by-8 plus AND-1 pair exists solely to isolate one bit, and the model test pins that bit 8 and not bit 0 is the one reported.

The inlined duplicate at 0x00b8d9ff is the strongest available evidence and it upgrades the claim from 'a dword field' to 'a packed flag word': the same function reads bit 8 of +0x2c and then reads bit 11 of +0x2c in the same basic block.

Because the extraction is a pure read with no side effect, 25 direct call sites can consult it freely, and 0x00c484e0 consults it twice on two different sub-objects within one function at 0x00c4852f and 0x00c48548.

The caller-side state guard at receiver+0x28 (values 0 and 1 skip the flag entirely) shows the flag word is only meaningful from state 2 onwards, so +0x28 and +0x2c together form a state-plus-flags pair.
AND AL,1 rather than AND EAX,1 is what makes the upper three bytes of the return provably zero; the model test therefore pins a full dword of 0 or 1 rather than a boolean.
The 0x00c8b8xx run of eight short functions in one code region all consult this flag on elements of pointer vectors, which is consistent with a per-element eligibility test in a container sweep.

The briefing recorded 25 callers; the live xref query returns 31 UNCONDITIONAL_CALL references, so three further callsites at 0x00c56f3f, 0x00c56f95 and 0x01025ad7 exist outside any Ghidra function body. None is a DATA reference, so the function still occupies no vtable slot.
unresolved_questions: What class owns this function? 31 live references, all UNCONDITIONAL_CALL, and no DATA reference, so it is not a vtable slot and no owner can be named.
What does flag bit 8 mean? That it is a flag is established; its game meaning is not, and no SDK field, global name or string ties it to a concept.
Which other bits of the word at +0x2c are in use? Only bit 8 (here) and bit 11 (0x00b8da12) were observed; the other 30 bits are unaccounted for.
Who writes the flag word at +0x2c? No writer was found in this batch.
What is the state enum at +0x28, and what are all its values beyond the observed 0, 1 and 2-or-greater?
What is 0x00b8d9b0, the chain of five calls that runs only when both bit 8 and bit 0x800 are clear? It was not resolved in this batch.
What are the three unreported callsites at 0x00c56f3f, 0x00c56f95 and 0x01025ad7, which lie outside any Ghidra function body?
No original-process trace exists, so the runtime flag values are unverified.
